name: Blepharospasm-Oromandibular Dystonia Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Blepharospasm-Oromandibular Dystonia Syndrome

criteria.description: Involuntary, bilateral, synchronous orbicularis oculi muscle spasms causing forced eyelid closure
Sustained or intermittent involuntary contractions of masticatory, lower facial, and tongue muscles causing jaw opening, closing, or deviation
No evidence of neurodegenerative disease or structural brain lesions on imaging
Symptoms persisting for at least 3 months
Exclusion of secondary dystonia causes such as drug-induced or metabolic etiologies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of both blepharospasm and oromandibular dystonia symptoms with exclusion of secondary causes and neurodegenerative diseases
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical; electrophysiological and imaging studies assist in exclusion of mimics

pathognomonic.symptomName: Bilateral involuntary orbicularis oculi muscle spasms
searchTerms: involuntary eyelid muscle spasms on both sides

pathognomonic.symptomName: Sustained or intermittent oromandibular muscle contractions causing jaw dystonia
Forced eyelid closure leading to functional blindness

common.symptomName: Speech difficulties due to oromandibular dystonia
searchTerms: speech problems from jaw muscle spasms
difficulty talking due to oromandibular dystonia
speech impairment from mouth muscle contractions

common.symptomName: Dry eyes secondary to impaired blinking
searchTerms: eye dryness due to reduced blinking
lack of tears caused by blinking problems

common.symptomName: Jaw pain or discomfort related to dystonic contractions

occasional.symptomName: Blepharospasm exacerbated by stress or bright light
Difficulty chewing due to jaw dystonia
searchTerms: difficulty biting due to jaw tightness

occasional.symptomName: Neck muscle involvement causing cervical dystonia
Mild anxiety related to social embarrassment

rare.symptomName: Sensory tricks (geste antagoniste) temporarily relieving dystonia
searchTerms: temporary relief from muscle spasms by touching
low mood related to ongoing health problems

rare.symptomName: Bleeding or bruising from repetitive muscle contractions
searchTerms: skin bruises caused by muscle tightness

laboratory: Exclusion of metabolic or drug-induced causes
imaging: Normal brain MRI excluding structural lesions
Functional imaging may show basal ganglia involvement
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified; some familial cases reported
other: Response to botulinum toxin injections supports diagnosis

distinguishingFeatures: Less frequent jaw or tongue dystonia
History of neuroleptic or dopamine antagonist use
Presence of metabolic or structural brain abnormalities
Presence of parkinsonism features such as bradykinesia and rigidity
Dystonia often asymmetric and associated with other extrapyramidal signs

redFlags: Rapid progression of symptoms over weeks
Presence of cognitive decline or other neurodegenerative signs
Unilateral dystonia with focal neurological deficits
references: Defazio G, Hallett M. Blepharospasm and oromandibular dystonia: clinical and pathophysiological features. Mov Disord. 2013;28(7):926-933.
Jinnah HA, Factor SA. Diagnosis and treatment of dystonia. Neurol Clin. 2015;33(1):77-100.
